newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Store sales data, Chicago PMI.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Store sales data, Chicago PMI.

text.p: Weekly store sales data, a measure of manufacturing activity in the Chicago area and new home sales figures for November will guide U.S. Treasury prices on Tuesday before trading ends early on New Year's Eve.
Activity is expected to be light on the last trading session of 1996 and instead of closing at 1700 EST/2200 GMT, as usual, the market will close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
U.S. financial markets will be closed on January 1 for the New Year's Day holiday.
"Probably the home sales number and the two retail sales numbers will get the market's attention," said Bill Hornbarger, fixed-income strategist at A.G. Edwards & Sons.

The BTM/Schroders weekly chain and department store sales data for the week ended December 28 come out at 0900 EST/1400 GMT. The Lynch Jones & Ryan Redbook report on store sales for the same period will come out at 1455 EST/1955 GMT, after the market has closed.
"I think people are still trying to get a gauge on how Christmas shopping went," said Hornbarger.

"The press reports that came out on sales activity right around Christmas were on the disappointing side," noted Daiwa Securities America Inc chief economist Michael Moran. "Sales did not seem as vigorous as they did in the early part of December. That's quite different from the pattern you saw in previous years. Retailers were disappointed in what they saw right around Christmas."

On Friday, for instance, the department store chain of Nordstrom Inc said its holiday same-store sales declined from last year and that its fourth-quarter earnings would be below Wall Street expectations.
Moran said he expected an increase in the BTM/Schroders store sales index, but only a small one.
For Redbook, "You should not be surprised at another slight downward revision to the monthly estimate," he said.

Market participants expected to see a bounce in November new home sales in line with increases reflected in other November housing market data, including the modest rise reported on Monday in November existing home sales to an annualized 4.04 million from an annualized 3.97 million in October.
"We expect a rise in new home sales, but unless it's quite large, I don't think it will shock the market," said David Sloan, senior economist at consulting firm I.D.E.A. Inc.
The new home sales data are due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
Also set for release at 1000 EST/1500 GMT on Tuesday are the December Chicago Purchasing Managers Index and the Conference Board's December consumer confidence index.

"The market will look at the Chicago Purchasing Managers survey for clues to the National (Association of) Purchasing Management's (NAPM) index," said Josh Feinman, vice president and global markets economist at Bankers Trust.
The NAPM is due on the Thursday after New Year's Day.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast, on average, a slip in the Chicago PMI to 55.6 in December from 57.6 in November.
"I lean toward a slight downward movement," said Moran. "The last (Chicago PMI) reading was fairly firm."
In late trade on Monday, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off slightly in thin trade, priced at 99-14/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
Market participants said the fact that most players have closed their books for the year made it highly unlikely that the market would budge from its current narrow range.
(( -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1679 ))
